Boundaries of the BOIN-ET Design

Source: R/boin_et_boundary.R
boin_et_boundary.Rd

Find the lower and upper DLT boundaries and the lower response boundary of the BOIN-ET design of Takeda, Taguri and Morita (2018). The three boundaries minimize the probability of an incorrect dose assignment under six hypotheses about the DLT and response probabilities at the current dose, and are searched on a grid of step 0.01, as in the 'boinet' package.

Usage

boin_et_boundary(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  prior = rep(1/6, 6)
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, for example 0.30.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target response probability, for example 0.60.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.1 * target, the value recommended by Takeda et al. (2018), which is far below the 0.6 * target of the BOIN design.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

p_saf_resp

Numeric scalar. Highest response probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target_resp.

prior

Numeric vector of length 6. Prior probabilities of the six hypotheses. Defaults to rep(1 / 6, 6), the noninformative choice of the article. The third hypothesis, under which every decision is correct, does not enter the criterion.

Value

An object of class boin_et_boundary, which is a list with components

lambda1

Lower DLT boundary. The dose is escalated when the observed DLT rate is at most lambda1 and the observed response rate is at most eta1.

lambda2

Upper DLT boundary. The dose is de-escalated when the observed DLT rate is at least lambda2.

eta1

Lower response boundary.

prob_incorrect

The minimized probability of an incorrect decision.

target, target_resp, p_saf, p_tox, p_saf_resp, prior

The design parameters.

Details

The grids run from p_saf to target for lambda1, from target to p_tox for lambda2 and from p_saf_resp to target_resp for eta1, all by 0.01. At each grid point the probability of an incorrect decision is evaluated with binomial probabilities for 100 patients, and the first minimum in the order of the grids is returned. This is the search of boinet::gridoptim(), including its expression for the fourth hypothesis, and with the default design parameters and a target of 0.30 for the DLT and 0.60 for the response it gives the boundaries 0.14, 0.35 and 0.48 reported by Takeda et al. (2018).

References

Takeda, K., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2018). BOIN-ET: Bayesian optimal interval design for dose finding based on both efficacy and toxicity outcomes. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 17(4), 383-395. doi:10.1002/pst.1864

Yamaguchi, Y., Takeda, K. and Maruo, K. (2025). boinet: An R Package for Bayesian Optimal Interval Design for Dose Finding Based on Both Efficacy and Toxicity Outcomes. The R Journal, 17(2), 15-34. doi:10.32614/RJ-2025-012

See also

boin_et_decision_table, sim_boin_et

Examples

bd <- boin_et_boundary(target = 0.30, target_resp = 0.60)
bd
#> BOIN-ET boundaries
#>   target DLT rate      : 0.3
#>   target response rate : 0.6
#>   p_saf / p_tox        : 0.03 / 0.42
#>   p_saf_resp           : 0.36
#> 
#>   lambda1 (escalate)   : 0.14
#>   lambda2 (de-escalate): 0.35
#>   eta1 (response)      : 0.48
#>   probability of an incorrect decision: 0.04703

c(bd$lambda1, bd$lambda2, bd$eta1)
#> [1] 0.14 0.35 0.48
